newsitem.title: USA: R.I. manufacturing job loss continues - economist.
newsitem.headline: R.I. manufacturing job loss continues - economist.

text.p: Rhode Island continues to lose jobs in key manufacturing industries and will trail both the nation and New England region in terms of employment and job growth, Sara Johnson, chief regional economist for DRI/McGraw Hill said Friday.

Johnson, speaking to a group of state officials, said Rhode Island's main manufacturing industries -- jewelry, silverware, textiles, toys, shipbuilding and metal products -- have all suffered significant losses in employment and market share over the past decade.
Manufacturing jobs in the state fell 3.0 percent in 1996 and is expected to decline another 1.2 percent annually over the next five years.
"Rhode Island faces a return to sluggish growth this spring, as layoffs continue in key manufacturing industries," Johnson said.

The state's per capita income of $24,900 in 1996 was 2.7 percent higher than the national per capita income, but 13.2 percent below New Englands, she said. The state average wages are also well below the region's.

Johnson estimated that, for the rest of this decade, service industries such as business services, education, health care and tourism will provide two-thirds of Rhode island's new jobs, with services employment expected to rise an average of 2.2 percent a year through 2000, trailing the nation's 3.0 percent pace.
She noted Rhode Island had taken several steps to make it more attractive to businesses including tax incentives to attract financial service companies as well as electricity deregulation.
